shots.line: This guy traded a single paper clip... for an entire house. And no, this is not a joke.
shots.scene: golden sunset over a prairie village with a red grain elevator; Kyle stands in front of a white house holding up a giant red paper clip

shots.line: See, Kyle MacDonald was sitting at his computer in two thousand five, with a red paper clip on his desk. And then he had a crazy idea. What if he kept trading that paper clip... for something just a little bit better? So he put it online.
shots.scene: a sunny apartment: Kyle at his computer, a red paper clip on the desk; lightbulb idea; he posts TRADE ME: ONE RED PAPER CLIP online

shots.line: And two women actually traded him a pen shaped like a fish. Kyle traded the pen for a doorknob with a smiley face. The doorknob became a camping stove. The stove became a generator.
shots.scene: sunny suburban street: Kyle walks along the sidewalk; at each trader (two women, a man, a family, a guy in a garage) a puff of sparkle and the item in his hand becomes the next one

shots.line: And then the trades got bigger and bigger. A snowmobile. A trip into the mountains. Even a delivery truck.
shots.scene: bright snowy mountain road: Kyle zooms along on a red snowmobile, then a ticket pops up, then he drives a white delivery truck with TRADE ME! on the side

shots.line: His story spread across the internet... and suddenly, everyone wanted to be part of it. A recording contract. A year of free rent. An afternoon with a rock star.
shots.scene: sunny suburb: Kyle stands on his parked TRADE ME! truck while neighbours crowd around filming with phones; notification bubbles pop; then cards fly in: record contract, a year of free rent, an afternoon with a rock star

shots.line: And after fourteen trades, the unbelievable happened. A small town in Canada offered him a real house. In return, the town got a role in a real movie... and held auditions for it.
shots.scene: sunset prairie village with a red grain elevator: Kyle walks up the road to a white house where the mayor hands him the key; townsfolk line up at an AUDITIONS sign

shots.line: Kyle never bought that house. He traded his way there... one paper clip at a time.
shots.scene: golden hour: Kyle on the porch of his house holds up a tiny red paper clip and smiles; the camera pulls back as the whole trade chain appears in an arc in the sky
